vision.tagline: The 20% of work that drives 80% of income — and the quality standards that make it worth paying for.

items.text: Get players to pay. Marketing, conversion, pricing, packaging. Every dollar funds payroll, royalties to Marvel and Upper Deck, cloud bills, and the next round of content. No sales = no business.
New sets, schemes, heroes. Content is the product. Content drives purchases and retention.
Reliability, matchmaking, reconnection. Churn kills recurring revenue.

sections.heading: Quality Standards
sections.tagline: How we do the above well — guardrails, not goals.

items.text: Exact rules of Marvel Legendary; no simplifications, no digital-only shortcuts.
Same card images, names, text, and semantics as the physical cards.
No hidden modifiers; verifiably fair randomness; no decisions made on behalf of players.
Tabletop cooperative experience; reliable sync, reconnection, late-joining.
Built for decades of expansions; core systems scale without rewrites.
The game must be **financially self-sustaining** from launch onward.
Revenue models protect gameplay fairness — no pay-to-win — and pricing, packaging, and distribution are open commercial decisions.
A non-negotiable royalty portion flows directly to Upper Deck and Marvel on every revenue stream.
If revenue falls short, non-essential features scale back **before** any compromise to rules, fairness, accessibility, or royalties.
